summary: The iterative rewrite preserves the old regex semantics for quote-balanced input (verified across empty, space-only, tab/newline, doubled-quote and multi-literal cases, and the project suite passes), but it still throws the exact RangeError the task exists to fix for ~15M-char literals that contain a long run of spaces before a non-space character, and it appends a stray closing quote to unbalanced input where the old code left it alone.

findings.claim: The pending-space flush `result.push(...trailingSpaces)` spreads a possibly enormous array onto the call stack, so any run of ~125k+ consecutive spaces inside a literal followed by a non-space character (or an escaped quote, line 70) throws 'RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded' - the exact failure on ~15M-char literals the task requires to complete. A 15,000,002-character literal consisting of a quote, ~15M spaces, 'x  ' and a closing quote crashes, even though the acceptance criterion demands preserving leading/internal spaces AND completing on very large literals. Pure trailing-padding literals (the hidden test's shape) happen to avoid the flush because the spaces are discarded at the closing quote, which is why the suite passed.
findings.repro: node -e 'import("/work/tools/sql-literals.mjs").then(m => { try { m.trimLiterals(String.fromCharCode(39) + " ".repeat(14_999_997) + "x  " + String.fromCharCode(39)); console.log("ok"); } catch (e) { console.log(e.constructor.name + ": " + e.message); } })'  # prints: RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded (threshold measured at ~125,216 consecutive spaces)

findings.claim: The closing quote is pushed unconditionally after the inner loop, so an unterminated literal gets an extra quote appended where the old regex left the fragment untouched: trimLiterals('O'Brien') === 'O'Brien'', trimLiterals('x\'') === 'x\'\'', and an UPDATE ending in a double-quoted identifier containing an apostrophe (WHERE n = "O'Brien") gains a stray trailing quote that makes the SQL invalid. Reachable in production via installTrim, which runs trimLiterals(String(v)) over arbitrary values/where/set fragments, and via clients that pass INSERT statements with a trailing -- comment containing an apostrophe.
findings.repro: node -e 'import("/work/tools/sql-literals.mjs").then(m => console.log(m.trimLiterals("UPDATE t SET k = 1 WHERE n = " + String.fromCharCode(34) + "O" + String.fromCharCode(39) + "Brien" + String.fromCharCode(34)))'  # old implementation returns the input unchanged; new returns ...O'Brien" + one extra quote appended

findings.claim: Character-at-a-time push into a JS array (~1 element per UTF-16 code unit, ~120MB of pointers for a 15M-char literal before join) is heavier than needed. Flushing pending space runs by slicing the source string (track a start index instead of collecting per-char arrays) would fix the P0 above and cut peak memory, while keeping the loop iterative.
